"Third call about the same problem."
"Nobody called me back."
"I'll go elsewhere."

These sentences exist in every company's tools.
What is missing is the time to read them at scale.

A manager sees a handful of difficult cases each week.
Not the thousands of conversations where frustration slowly builds.

So the departure looks like a surprise.
When it had been announced, often several times.

How many of your customers told you before they left?

26 years. Next-day delivery. One-click payment. Free returns.
And satisfaction has barely moved.

Peak: 84 in 2003.
Lowest: 77 in 2001 and 2021.

Every improvement quickly becomes the new normal.
What delighted customers yesterday merely meets expectations today.

And a score has a limit:
it measures a level, not a cause.

79/100 does not tell you whether customers complain about delivery,
return fees, product quality or reaching support.

Their reviews, tickets and calls do.

To break the plateau, doing better in general is not enough.
You need to know exactly what still disappoints.

Waiting between contacts.
Explaining the problem again.

These pain points sit between channels.
And they are often what makes customers leave.

planning.title: 77 % du chiffre d'affaires hôtelier mondial se fait désor… (FR)
planning.text:
𝟳𝟳 % 𝗱𝘂 𝗰𝗵𝗶𝗳𝗳𝗿𝗲 𝗱'𝗮𝗳𝗳𝗮𝗶𝗿𝗲𝘀 𝗵𝗼̂𝘁𝗲𝗹𝗶𝗲𝗿 𝗺𝗼𝗻𝗱𝗶𝗮𝗹 𝘀𝗲 𝗳𝗮𝗶𝘁 𝗱𝗲́𝘀𝗼𝗿𝗺𝗮𝗶𝘀 𝗲𝗻 𝗹𝗶𝗴𝗻𝗲.

C'était 66 % en 2017.
Plus de 80 % sont attendus d'ici 2030.

Avant de réserver, le client lit.
Les photos.
Les prix.
Et surtout les avis.

55 % des voyageurs de loisirs placent le rapport qualité-prix en premier (fin 2024).
Mais le rapport qualité-prix ne se juge pas sur le prix seul.
Il se juge sur ce que les autres clients racontent.

Deux hôtels au même tarif ne se valent pas
si l'un accumule les remarques sur le bruit
et l'autre les compliments sur l'accueil.

Vos avis sont votre vitrine.
Et une mine d'informations sur ce qui fait monter ou baisser votre note.

Les suivez-vous comme un indicateur de gestion ?

Source : Statista, dossier Hotels (2026), données 2024

planning.title: 51% of customers dislike chatbots because they keep them … (EN)
planning.text:
𝟱𝟭% 𝗼𝗳 𝗰𝘂𝘀𝘁𝗼𝗺𝗲𝗿𝘀 𝗱𝗶𝘀𝗹𝗶𝗸𝗲 𝗰𝗵𝗮𝘁𝗯𝗼𝘁𝘀 𝗯𝗲𝗰𝗮𝘂𝘀𝗲 𝘁𝗵𝗲𝘆 𝗸𝗲𝗲𝗽 𝘁𝗵𝗲𝗺 𝗳𝗿𝗼𝗺 𝗮 𝗿𝗲𝗮𝗹 𝗽𝗲𝗿𝘀𝗼𝗻.

That was in 2018.
The bots have improved since.
The need has not changed.

In 2022, 61% said chatting with an agent was the easiest customer service channel.
Only 23% chose video.

People like chat.
They want a person behind it.

Bots still help for simple tasks (2024):
→ almost half used them to book appointments
→ about 47% to place orders
→ 46% to report an issue

And in 2025, 32% of furniture shoppers felt a chatbot informed them as well as an associate.
Two thirds still did not.

A chatbot does not end the conversation.
It records part of it.

Where customers give up.
When they ask for a human.
What they could not solve.

That is data about your customers.
Is anyone reading it?

Source: Statista, Customer service in the U.S., AI and XR in e-commerce, AI in U.S. e-commerce dossiers

→ Full article in comments

#Chatbots #CustomerService #CustomerExperience #AI #CustovoxAI

planning.title: 88 % des clients attendent un espace d'aide en ligne. (FR)
planning.text:
𝟴𝟴 % 𝗱𝗲𝘀 𝗰𝗹𝗶𝗲𝗻𝘁𝘀 𝗮𝘁𝘁𝗲𝗻𝗱𝗲𝗻𝘁 𝘂𝗻 𝗲𝘀𝗽𝗮𝗰𝗲 𝗱'𝗮𝗶𝗱𝗲 𝗲𝗻 𝗹𝗶𝗴𝗻𝗲.

C'était déjà le cas en 2018 aux États-Unis.
Ce n'est plus un bonus, c'est un minimum.

Autres chiffres du même dossier :
→ 49 % commencent leur démarche en ligne (2017)
→ 18 % : le plus frustrant est de ne pas pouvoir résoudre seuls (2018)
→ 13 % citent l'information désorganisée comme premier problème (2018)

Le cercle vicieux :
le client cherche, ne trouve pas, s'agace,
puis appelle, déjà irrité.

Le volume de contacts monte.
Les délais s'allongent.
Et personne ne sait ce qui manque dans la FAQ.

Pourtant la réponse est là.
Dans les tickets.

Chaque question posée au service client
indique une information absente, introuvable ou peu claire.

Les questions qui reviennent le plus
désignent exactement quoi écrire.

Source : Statista, dossier Customer service in the U.S. (2025)

#ServiceClient #SelfService #FAQ #ExperienceClient #CustovoxAI

planning.title: Mobile voice revenue is falling 2.72% a year (2023-2028 f… (EN)
planning.text:
𝗠𝗼𝗯𝗶𝗹𝗲 𝘃𝗼𝗶𝗰𝗲 𝗿𝗲𝘃𝗲𝗻𝘂𝗲 𝗶𝘀 𝗳𝗮𝗹𝗹𝗶𝗻𝗴 𝟮.𝟳𝟮% 𝗮 𝘆𝗲𝗮𝗿 (𝟮𝟬𝟮𝟯-𝟮𝟬𝟮𝟴 𝗳𝗼𝗿𝗲𝗰𝗮𝘀𝘁).

From $396.6B in 2016
to $264.4B in 2022
to about $224.6B in 2028.

People call less.
Routine conversations moved to messaging.

So which calls remain?

The ones where writing is not enough.
A complex situation.
An urgent problem.
A worry. A dispute.

For customer service, every call now carries higher stakes.
The customer who picks up the phone has often tried something else first.

And it is still a key channel:
54% of Americans prefer the phone to solve a customer service problem (2022).

Yet most calls are recorded and never listened to again.

Fewer calls.
More important calls.
Rarely understood.

Source: Statista Market Insights (2023), Mobile Voice
